column1: # Vendor documentation pages this package cites, and what each one DID when a person read
# it. Checked by `script/check_doc_sources.sh`; see that script's header for why this is
# status-and-destination rather than a content diff, and why a redirect is the signal.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   url  expect_status  expect_location  observed_on  class  note
# `expect_location` is `-` when the page does not redirect. It is never left blank: TAB is
# IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs collapses into one delimiter and every later column
# shifts. The first draft of this file did leave it blank and the checker reported all
# seven rows as changed.
# `class` is `auto` (a machine can verify this) or `manual` (it cannot — a human must
# re-read it, and the row goes STALE to force that). Every row here is `auto`: this
# vendor publishes its documentation anonymously, which not every venue in this family
# does.
# Do not edit a row to make the check pass. The row records what someone READ; rewriting
# it to match a fetch nobody looked at turns this file into a rubber stamp.
https://developer.webull.com/apis/docs/rate-limits/
column6: THE load-bearing page: the per-endpoint rate-limit table capabilities/0's ceilings come from. Added by the vendor 2026-08-14 and missed until 2026-09-09.

column1: https://developer.webull.com/apis/docs/market-data-api/faq/
column6: States 300 requests per 60 seconds, which the per-endpoint table above contradicts by 5x. Watched BECAUSE it is wrong: if the vendor corrects it, that resolves a known self-contradiction.

column1: https://developer.webull.com/apis/docs/market-data-api/data-streaming-api/
column6: MQTT-over-WebSocket contract, topic table and the 3 msg/sec/connection push rate Feed's sharding is built on.

column6: Batch order semantics behind Rest's @batch_limit of 50.

column6: The index. Diffing THIS is the one mechanism that has ever caught a real vendor change in this family — the rate-limits page was listed here from 2026-08-14.
